title: Causeway shafts are waterproof and hold air, not water
summary: Filippo tells of Causeway shafts are waterproof and hold air, not water, about present at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And I tell you that for me the shafts are waterproof. It means that the water that is the water level if you if you if you can see the water level that is outside the shafts, the water is not able to go inside the shafts.

plain: A researcher named Filippo talks about shafts cut into the rock beneath the causeway, an ancient stone road on the Giza plateau in Egypt where the great pyramids stand. He says the shafts are waterproof: water stands outside them but cannot get in, so they hold air instead. He tells it as a sign that the shafts were deliberately built as part of a planned system, not just holes in the ground.
